gap: No result ChatGPT got says that the TerraMaster N5095 boxes it recommended (F2-425, F4-425, F2-423, F4-423) are Jasper Lake chips. Jellyfin's own hardware guide tells buyers to avoid that class of chip ('Intel J/M/N/Y series low power CPUs up to 11th gen'). Jellyfin's Intel guide also says Jasper Lake can only encode in Low-Power mode, which needs HuC firmware and a manual setup step. Alder Lake-N chips (12th-gen N series, such as the N100 in the DXP2800) support both encoding modes on Linux by default. So TerraMaster's '4K H.264/H.265 transcoding' claim for the N5095 and UGREEN's Quick Sync claim for the N100 do not mean the same thing.
standout_why: Both Jellyfin docs were in ChatGPT's results and some chats cited them: the hardware-selection page was cited in five chats and the GitHub intel.md in one. Those pages contain the general rules ('avoid J/M/N/Y up to 11th gen'; 'Gen 11 JSL/EHL graphics - Only support LP encoding mode'; HuC setup needed for Jasper Lake). But they name no NAS. Of the review pages, itechguides and computingforgeeks/best-2-bay identify the F2-425 and F4-425 as N5095, but neither applies the avoid rule or mentions LP-only or HuC encoding. Computingforgeeks even repeats TerraMaster's 4K60 H.264/H.265 rating as a positive. Starry Hope's best-2-bay and ubnas don't mention the N5095 or the LP mode at all. ChatGPT cited the Jellyfin page in every chat and still recommended N5095 TerraMasters as the 'budget' or '4-bay' pick. That makes the gap a mapping (this chip is on Jellyfin's avoid list, here is why) rather than a fact nobody has published. A second, smaller finding is new to ChatGPT's result set. The 'F2-425 Plus' is sold in two CPU versions: N150 at $499.99 list and N95 at $399.49 list, both per Starry Hope's model page, which gives no price date. Starry Hope's best-2-bay page, which ChatGPT got, describes only the N150. ChatGPT's cards showed both chips under the same name at $375.99 and $399.49 and said 'verify the CPU revision'.
decides: This confirms the DXP2800 (N100) as the pick and removes the whole N5095 tier (F2-425, F4-425, F2-423, F4-423) from 'budget alternative' slots for Jellyfin transcoding. Jellyfin's guide says to avoid that chip class, and its encoder depends on a firmware setup step that has to be done by hand on Jasper Lake. Whether TerraMaster's TOS already does that step is unverified. Under $400, the only TerraMaster that stays a Jellyfin alternative is the F2-425 Plus N95 version, a 2023 N-series chip in the same family as the N100. The page should name that variant explicitly, because the N150 version lists at $499.99 per Starry Hope.

findings.label: Jellyfin's hardware guidance on low-power Intel chips
findings.value: Recommends 'Intel N100' and 'Intel 12th gen or above N series platforms'. Says 'Intel J/M/N/Y series low power CPUs up to 11th gen use a different architecture … It is advised to avoid using these parts in a Jellyfin Server.'
findings.note: The page doesn't name the N5095, J4125 or N4505. They fall under 'N/J series up to 11th gen' because they are 10th-gen-class Jasper Lake or Gemini Lake parts, and Jellyfin's Intel guide calls Jasper Lake '10th Gen Pentium/Celeron/Atom'. That covers the TerraMaster F2-425, F4-425, F2-423 and F4-423 (N5095), the Synology DS225+ (J4125) and the QNAP TS-262 (N4505). The same page also recommends 8 GB RAM for an integrated-graphics server; the N5095 TerraMasters ship with 4 GB.

findings.label: Encoder mode: Jasper Lake vs Alder Lake-N
findings.value: 'Gen 11 JSL/EHL graphics - Only support LP encoding mode.' 'Low-Power encoding can offload the GPU usage with the help of the HuC firmware.' 'The setup is not necessary unless you are using an Intel Jasper Lake or Elkhart Lake processor.' 'Linux supports two modes only on Gen 12 ADL+ by default.' 'GuC & HuC firmware can be missing on older distros.'
findings.source_title: Jellyfin docs: Intel hardware acceleration (intel.md, master)
findings.note: This is the source behind the table footnote. On N5095 (Jasper Lake), hardware H.264/HEVC encoding works only in Low-Power mode, which depends on a manual setup step on Jasper Lake. On Alder Lake-N (N100, N95; the N150 is Twin Lake per ITPro), Linux supports both modes by default. This is the same file as the github.com/jellyfin/jellyfin.org/blob/... page ChatGPT cited in one chat.

findings.value: 'Decoding AV1 8/10-bit - Gen 12 Tiger Lake (11th Gen Core) and newer'. 'Jasper Lake and Elkhart Lake processors are 10th Gen Pentium/Celeron/Atom, which don't have AV1 acceleration.'
findings.source_title: Jellyfin docs: Intel hardware acceleration (intel.md, master)
findings.note: ChatGPT's tables already said 'AV1 decode: N100 yes / N5095 no', so this isn't new. It's included for completeness of the normalised table.

findings.label: HDR tone-mapping support by generation
findings.value: 'Hardware accelerated HDR/DV to SDR tone-mapping is supported on all Intel GPUs that have HEVC 10-bit decoding' (Gemini Lake and newer).
findings.source_title: Jellyfin docs: Intel hardware acceleration (intel.md, master)
findings.note: This normalises ChatGPT's 'HDR tone mapping: Yes vs setup-dependent' column. Both chip families support it, so the real difference is the encoder mode in the finding above. The same doc says LP encoding 'can be useful for speeding up the OpenCL based HDR/DV tone-mapping'.
